about: DATA for tools/decide-with-a-method. `records`: where the person's own decision records are: the methods they decide with (the branch nodes of their one Checks list, `method_list`, row type `method_row`, the rows matching `method_where`, one per method: its id, name, steps, switches, backbone, decision fields and voice; a method is `method_link` the method it builds on (until the rows are rewritten, a row with no `method_link` is read by the first of `old_method_links` it has: a branch's old `extends`, a check's old `method`), up to a root, one link in place of `extends`) and their checks (rows of `check_list`, row type `check_row`, one per check: its id, the step it sharpens, the method it is `method_link`, its switch, its question and what a good answer does); a call reads a method's rows by id (`record:check:<id>`): the method it names or its decision was opened with, else `default_method`, then each method it is `method_link`, up to its root, so it costs the depth of the method tree, never the size of the list (only an account with neither row lists its rows matching `method_where`); and only the checks of the step it asks or judges, each by id: the ids its step lists in `step_parts_field` and in `check_ids` (a step that lists no parts yet is read by the door's `where` on `check_step_field`), and a question sends each check as its id and question, its whole words (good answer, refusals) coming by id on request, at most `most_explained` ids at once, a decision's answered steps (`step` + <decision id> + ':' + its number, `step_digits` wide; a logged call likewise under `call`, `call_digits` wide) and a decision opened from a source (`case_prefix` + the source id in base64url). `precedence`: who the current outcome of a decision belongs to when the person and a check disagree (read-data/decision-outcome.mjs): with person_confirmed_wins true a later check never replaces the person's own confirmed report; false, the newest current evidence wins. `similar`: how earlier decisions are brought back when a similar one comes up (read-data/similar-decisions.mjs): the newest `look_back` decisions in `order` (a declared order of the engine's decision records, newest first) are weighed by the words of `word` (a regular expression, matched in lower case) their goals share with this one, plus `same_method` when they were made with the same method; a decision whose method is not named was made with `default_method`. Those scoring more than `above` are kept, closest first, `limit` of them unless the caller asks for fewer or more, never more than `most`. `pursuits`: the person's pursuits travel with the questions whose step ids are in `with_steps`, the newest `carried` of them, found among at most `scan`. `most_cited_refs`: how many different references one answer may cite. `grader`: who judges each check (the calling AI, on its own subscription: `self` or `second-judge`) and the words it is given. `words`: what Trillion says at each moment of a decision ({name} is filled from the decision) and every refusal. `share`: how a decided decision is made safe to show strangers (tool:share-a-decision): the person's never-publish phrases are rows of row type `never_publish_row` (field `never_publish_field`); a rewrite has the `entry_fields` (words, or a list of words); `rewrite` is what the calling AI is told; the plain privacy pass (tools/learn-from-everyones-results) must find nothing in it, then `check_tool` must accept it under the `reidentification` rubric (a true-or-false question, synthetic calibration cases, accepted only when the answer is false), bound to exactly that rewrite; the kept entry is then sent to `pool_tool`. `records.version` and `records.version_digits`: how a superseded version of an answered step is named beside the step (`decision-step:<id>:<nnn>:v<vvv>`); the step's own record holds its current version. `revision`: the words a revision's `because` needs (`because_min_words`, `because_max_words`), who a revision is by when the caller does not say (`by`), and how long that name may be. `evidence.most_per_call`: how many evidence rows one add carries. `history.most_versions`: how many versions of a step its history returns, the newest. `writes` and `write_bytes`: how many records and bytes of their JSON one door write carries (the engine's cap, and room under its 64 KiB message); a decision laid apart in one change that needs more is written in parts, its root last. `records.laid_apart`: every list of a decision that grows as it grows, each kept as one record per item (`type` + ':' + <decision id> + ':' + its number, `digits` wide) with its length in the root's `counts`: evidence rows, answered steps' summaries, candidates, reported results, carried-out receipts, earlier decisions and cited pursuits (read-data/decision-records.mjs). `records.method`: the record type of a method snapshot, kept once under its content identity (`decision-method:<identity>`) and named by the root's `method_identity`. `record_bytes`: the most bytes of one record's JSON this tool writes besides the root; a larger one is kept as its short fields and `kept_in_parts`, its whole value as text in records of `records.part.type` (<its key> + `part.suffix` + its number, `part.digits` wide), each under the bound. A root itself over `record_bytes` (an old-layout root with a large field) keeps its largest fields, largest first, as one value in parts (<its id> + ':root-fields' + `part.suffix` + its number) until it fits, names them in `fields_in_parts` with the number of parts in `root_fields_in_parts`, and reads them back on the root; its id, status, ending, times, source, method, input identity, counts and decision never move. `options`: the options stay on the root, so a new decision's options are bounded: at most `most` of them and `most_bytes` bytes of their JSON, or the start is refused (`words.options_too_large`). `records.laid_apart.options` names where a root written while options were laid apart keeps them; they are read back from there and folded into the root at its next change.

decision_id.description: The decision the person decided (from tool:start-a-decision)

option_id.description: The option the person chose, one of the decision's options

next_action.description: What you will do now to carry out the person's decision

success_measure.description: How you will both know it worked

person.description: Where the person said it: message_id names the message row they sent, and said is their exact words in it. From their own signed-in page, said alone (the page's run is the source).

said.description: The person's exact words, as they wrote them

message_id.description: The message row the person sent (type message, speaker person)

decision_id.description: The decision about to be made

source_id.description: Unique text naming where this decision comes from

method.description: The saved view over the person's method rows this decision is answered by (their default method view when left out)

parent_decision_id.description: A decision of the person's this one is a child of (never itself)

evidence.description: The rows to add: each { ref, claim } or { ref, from: { decision_id, ref } }

ref.description: A ref unique in this decision

observed_at.description: When it was seen, at or before now

rewrite.description: { situation, options: [words], chosen, why, measured_by }, written by the calling AI from the redacted facts

reidentification.description: The whole answer of tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict for the check this tool named

metadata_only.description: Answer only access, allowance and the no-pursuits words; read no row

native_collection_page.description: One bounded page with its coverage, instead of the whole what-helped view

before.description: The next_before an earlier page answered: the page starts below this created_at

access.description: What your computer reports: { capabilities: [names], limits?: { [access]: [{ count, per }] } }

allowance.description: What your computer reports of your decision allowance: { count, per, used }

space_pursuits.description: The pursuits your spaces share, shown beside your own

query.description: The route's query parameters, by name

body.description: The JSON body the page sent ({} when none)

browser.description: The asking browser's own facts: user_agent, origin, visitor

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

after.description: The next of the page before, to read on

limit.description: How many rows at most in this page

decision_id.description: The decision these answers are for

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

by.description: Who answered; the calling AI when not given

row.description: The id of a row of the method, as tool:read-a-method gave it

cites.description: Ids of rows of the method the answer rests on

evidence_refs.description: Refs of the decision's evidence the answer rests on

words.read_the_method: Read the method with tool:read-a-method (method {method}), a page at a time until next is null.
words.record_the_answers: Answer its rows with tool:record-method-answers: one call for as many rows as you can, each answer citing the rows of the method and the evidence of this decision it rests on (add evidence with tool:add-decision-evidence).
words.decide_when_answered: When every row has an answer, choose with tool:make-the-decision.
words.method_unanswered: Method {method} has {count} of its {rows} rows without an answer, the first of them {first}. Answer them with tool:record-method-answers, then decide.
words.ready: Every question is answered, so make the decision now with tool:make-the-decision, in this turn: a decision left open changes nothing. Choose the option the evidence supports and send its id from options as option_id. Leave a question to the person only when its answer is their own values, drive or budget, and then ask them that one question; settle every product, architecture, placement, naming or build question from the facts yourself, even when they have objected to every option.
words.resume: Do this now: {next_action}. How you will know it worked: {success_measure}. If it does not, bring back what actually happened: a failed result is a fact, and the fastest way to the right next move. Once it works, bring the larger change it makes possible as the next decision.
words.carry_out: Do this now, in this same turn: {next_action}. Then name the next step that doing it makes possible and do that too, until this is true: {success_measure}. When it is done, or you reach a wall you cannot get past, call tool:say-what-was-done with decision_id {case_id}: done with what happened, or the exact wall (the file, field, refused command or missing credential). Never end the turn with this step still to do, a list of follow-ups, or a question about whether to do it.
words.new_case: Give this decision a source_id (choose unique text; an existing conversation, message or file id is not required), goal (what is being decided), evidence (an array of {ref, claim}: the facts and every non-negotiable constraint) and, only if you already hold them, at least two options (each {id, label}); leave options out to let the method's steps generate and rule out the candidates. Correct the input and try again.
words.evidence_item: Each evidence item needs a unique ref and claim
words.option_item: Each option needs a unique id and label
words.options_too_large: A decision holds at most {count} options, {bytes} bytes of them in all: shorten their labels, or group similar options under one, and start it again.
words.method_name: method must name a method id
words.source_changed: Source {source_id} already has decision {case_id} with different content. Continue that decision with its id, or use a new source_id.
words.already_decided: This decision already has a decision. Revise one of its answers, with its reason, to reopen it, or report a failed result first.
words.from_self: from names this decision: to change its own answer, revise it instead.
words.parent_invalid: A parent decision has to be another of your decisions, and not this one.
words.from_not_found: No decision has that id to bring an answer or evidence from.
words.evidence_shape: Each evidence row needs a ref and either a claim, or from { decision_id, ref } to bring it in from another of your decisions.
words.evidence_count: Add from 1 to {count} evidence rows at a time.
words.evidence_ref_taken: Evidence {ref} already says something else in this decision: give the new row its own ref.
words.evidence_from_missing: That decision has no evidence {ref} to bring in.
words.decision_shape: Decision needs option, reason, next action, success measure, and evidence refs
words.generation_shape: expected_generation must name the positive decision generation being prepared
words.move_shape: move, when given, is the chosen move in words
words.generation_changed: The prepared decision generation changed. Read the current decision before continuing.
words.unknown_option: Decision names an unknown option ({option}): option_id is one of {options}
words.new_decision_needs_failure: A new decision needs a failed result, or a revised answer that reopens the decision.
words.person_verdict_shape: A person's own decision needs decision_id, option_id, next_action, success_measure and person: { said, message_id? }, where said is the person's exact words
words.person_verdict_no_person: Only the person decides without the method: name the message they sent (person.message_id, a message row where they are the speaker), or have them record it on their own signed-in page. An AI saying the person decided is not the person's verdict; to decide yourself, read the method (tool:read-a-method), record answers to its rows (tool:record-method-answers) and then call tool:make-the-decision
words.person_message_missing: No message {id} is kept in the person's records; name the message the person sent
words.person_message_not_theirs: Message {id} was said by {speaker}, not the person; only the person's own words decide without the method
words.person_words_not_said: The words in person.said are not in message {id}; quote the person exactly as they wrote it
words.person_decided_note: The person decided this themselves ({basis}, {at}): their words are the evidence, and the method was not walked ({steps} steps marked decided by the person)
words.decided_note: This decision was already made with these words; nothing changed.
words.result_shape: A result needs result (met, failed or unknown) and a summary
words.ask_the_person: Ask your person what happened and set answered_by to "person"
words.no_decision_yet: This decision has no decision yet
words.source_ref_shape: source_ref must name the original report
words.report_generation_shape: expected_generation must name the positive decision generation this report concerns
words.report_words_differ: This report source already has different words. Keep a new source_ref and name the original in supersedes to correct it.
words.stale_outcome: The decision changed while the result was being reported. Read the current decision before reporting it again.
words.supersedes_shape: supersedes must name an earlier report source in this decision generation
words.observed_at_shape: observed_at must be a time at or before now
words.said_shape: Say state (done or wall) and what_happened: what was done, or the exact wall (the file, field, refused command or missing credential)
words.said_generation_changed: The decision generation changed before its carried-out receipt. Read the current decision before continuing.
words.share_shape: A rewrite is { situation, options: [words], chosen, why, measured_by }, each one words, and nothing else.
words.share_not_safe: The rewrite could still point to someone: {found}. Rewrite those parts in general terms and send it again.
words.share_check: Ask {tool} whether these words could point to one person, with exactly this rubric and content, and send its whole answer back as reidentification.
words.end_shape: Name 1 to {most} decisions to end, each { decision_id, because } with its own decision_id, and by: who ends them
words.end_kept_open: A decision with status {status} has a result or a correction to keep; it is not ended.
words.end_changed: The decision changed after it was read; it is not ended. Read it again before ending it.
words.field_unknown: "{name}" is not a field of this call. The fields it declares are: {fields}.
words.field_misplaced: "{name}" belongs at the top level of the call, not inside "{in}".
words.end_too_large: The records door refused this decision's write as too large; it is not ended and is as it was.

share.rewrite: Rewrite this decision so no one could tell who made it. Remove or generalize every name, nickname, company, product, brand, place, event, date, month, age, number, job title, and any unusual detail that could point to one person. Say sizes and shares in words, never as figures, and never write [removed]; write around anything missing in plain general words. Keep the kind of situation, the choices, what was chosen, why, and how success is measured. Send it back as rewrite: { situation, options: [words], chosen, why, measured_by }.

reidentification.question: Could these words point to one specific person, company, product, brand, place, event or date, or carry a detail unusual enough to recognise? Ordinary words for common activities, roles and equipment do not.

means.yes: Something in the words could lead a reader to one particular person, business, place, event or date: a name, a precise place or time, a rank, a one-of-a-kind role, or a rare circumstance.
means.no: Every detail is general: it would fit many people, and nothing in it is rare or precise enough to recognise.

calibration.content: Dana Whitfield, who owns the Bluebird Bakery on Elm Street, chose to open a second shop in March.
The only paediatric surgeon on a small island chose to stop taking night shifts after her twins were born.
The founder of the country's largest chain of coffee shops chose to step down as its chief executive.
Someone with a steady job weighed starting a small business on the side and chose to keep the job while testing the idea on weekends.
A person deciding how to spend spare evenings chose a short course over a second part-time job, and counts it a success if they finish it.
A team lead chose to move a weekly meeting to every other week to give people more time to focus.

conflict._why: A case write refused as changed (original_command_conflict) is read again and written again under a fresh key, up to this many reads in all. The tool process is not given the run deadline, so this is not derived from it: it is four attempts, each one read and one write, where a write answers within the door's write bound (5 s, the bound writes are measured under in the decision-case notes).

candidates.about: A decision may open from its goal and evidence (its facts and every non-negotiable constraint) with no options, so no option list written in advance biases it. Then the answer list `field` of whichever method step asks it (the universal method's rule_out) is what still stands; each item becomes an option `id_prefix` + its position (or keeps its own { id, label }), and the decision chooses among those.

ending.about: tool:end-a-decision closes decisions no one will carry on: their status becomes `status`, and the status they had, when, who and why stay on the record beside every other field. A decision whose status is in `keeps_open` holds a checked result or a correction, so it is never ended. One call ends at most `most` decisions.

person_verdict._what: A decision the person made themselves, kept by tool:record-a-persons-own-decision (decisions.mjs recordAPersonsOwnDecision). Its only source is the person: a message row they sent (`message`: its row type, the field naming who spoke and the value that is the person, its words and time, and the roads that are their own signed-in page), or a run their own signed-in page started, which the engine attests as the task's origin (`page_origin`, trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/tool-runs.json page_origin: no input can set it and no AI key's run carries it). The basis names are old trillion's trusted person sources (src/check-uses.mjs personReportVerified). `evidence_ref` is the evidence row the person's words are kept as, numbered by the decision generation. `decided_by` marks the decision and its root, so a reader knows the method was not walked.
